ambiguity:
There are three alternative readings.
(a) Oct–Dec 2026 is FY2027. If the actual FY2027 minimum benefit of $25 (published after the 2026-07-03 freeze) is used, the total is $243 instead of $240.
(b) I could not open the DES manual to confirm the March 1, 2026 effective date of the 185% → 200% change; it comes from search-index text attributed to the DES change log. If 200% applied all year, the answer is 12 × $24 = $288. If 185% applied all year, the answer is $0, which matches the consensus. The USDA table updated 2026-06-29 shows 200% before the freeze.
(c) The two $298 premium fields may be one expense or two. Either way the medical deduction is too small to matter.

computation:
One-person SNAP household: Head, age 80 and disabled. Shelter costs: none listed (only a mortgage balance, no payments). Utilities: none listed.

1) Gross monthly income: Social Security $23,736/12 = $1,978.00. Pension $6,720/12 = $560.00. Dividends $16/12 = $1.33. Capital gains $72/12 = $6.00, which may be excluded as proceeds from selling a resource. Total is about $2,539–$2,545 a month.

2) Arizona broad-based categorical eligibility (BBCE, which Arizona calls Expanded Categorical Eligibility; 7 U.S.C. 2014(a), 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)): every household gets the TANF/MOE-funded referral on the application. The USDA BBCE table, updated 2026-06-29 (before the freeze), lists Arizona as "No limit on assets | 200%". Arizona's policy manual current page is titled "NA Expanded Categorical Eligibility Standard (200% …)". The archived text used 185%: when gross income "exceeds 185% of the current federal poverty level … the budgetary unit is not categorically eligible."
- The 185% → 200% change is recorded as effective 2026-03-01. I could not open the DES manual directly (HTTP 403); that date comes from search-index text attributed to the DES FAA5 change log.
- Jan–Feb 2026, at 185%: the limit is $15,650×1.85/12 = $2,413, or $2,461 using the 2026 guideline of $15,960. Income of about $2,540 is over both, so the household is not categorically eligible.
- Mar–Dec 2026, at 200%: the limit is $2,608 (2025 guideline) or $2,660 (2026 guideline). Income of about $2,540 is under both, so the household is categorically eligible. That means no asset test and no net income test.

3) Jan–Feb under regular rules: an elderly/disabled household skips the gross income test but must pass the net income test. Net income ≈ $2,545 − $209 standard deduction − at most about $31 excess medical ($796/yr ÷ 12 − $35) ≈ $2,305. That is above 100% of the poverty line (about $1,305), and assets of $58,700 exceed the $4,500 elderly/disabled limit. Benefit is $0.

4) Mar–Dec allotment (7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(A)): $298 maximum allotment − 30% × about $2,305 = negative. But 7 U.S.C. 2017(a) and 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(C) give every eligible one- or two-person household the minimum benefit. That is 8% × $298 = $23.84, rounded to $24 for FY2026 (Oct 2025–Sep 2026). The zero-benefit denial rule in (e)(2)(iii) covers only households of three or more.

5) Oct–Dec 2026 falls in FY2027. Those values (minimum benefit $25, maximum $306) were published after 2026-07-03. Under the frozen law, the FY2026 $24 carries forward.

Annual total under frozen law: 7 × $24 (Mar–Sep) + 3 × $24 (Oct–Dec) = $240. Using the FY2027 $25 for Oct–Dec gives $168 + $75 = $243. If 200% had applied all year, the total would be $288.

The consensus answer of $0 uses the old 185% limit, or regular rules for the whole year. It misses that the household is categorically eligible from March and that one-person households get the minimum benefit.
definition_reading: "Annual SNAP benefit amount" means the total SNAP allotment for the one-person SNAP household (Head) across calendar 2026: the sum of monthly allotments, with each month under the rules in force that month. Take-up of Arizona's TANF/MOE referral, which confers BBCE, is assumed under the prompt's take-up convention.
